If p <= R(m, n) - 1, alpha >= R(m-2, n)-1, beta >= R(m, n-2)-1, gamma >= R(m-1, n)-1 and delta >= R(m, n-1)-1, then (p - 1)(p - 2 - alpha) <= max over d in [p-1-delta, gamma] of (-3d^2 + (alpha - beta + 3(p - 1))d + (beta - alpha)(p - 1))', whose [4] is that Discrete Mathematics paper; and independently as Theorem 2.3 of a 2009 paper by Xiang, Qian and Fu, in solved form, citing the same paper. The 2009 closed form gives 1138.989624, floor 1138. Recomputing the whole HW+ column forward from non-HW+ cells only also yields 1138. The arithmetic is strong; the question this row asks is not settled.

rows.sourceRead: read in full and RECOMPUTED: the credited file (HTTP 200, 47,742 bytes) and the repository's READMEs. The file has one commit, 2020-05-04, which matches the survey's '(2020)'.
rows.evidence: The repository's graphs README defines the format: 'The file name *gXY.n* gives a 2-coloring of the edges of *K<sub>n</sub>* with no copy of *K<sub>X</sub>* colored 0, and no copy of *K<sub>Y</sub>* colored 1.' and 'In each file, the *i*th entry in the *j*th row gives the color assigned to the edge *(i,j)*.' The file was checked exhaustively by scripts/check-ramsey-coloring.mjs, committed with this reading: 218 rows of 218 characters in {0,1}, symmetric, 23,653 edges = C(218,2). Two independent exhaustive searches agree — a maximum-clique branch and bound and a complete enumeration of k-cliques — giving 'max clique in colour 0 = 6', 'number of K7 in colour 0 = 0', 'max clique in colour 1 = 7', 'number of K8 in colour 1 = 0', and 'RESULT: PASS -- no K7 in colour 0 and no K8 in colour 1 on n=218: R(7,8) > 218, i.e. R(7,8) >= 219'. A graph on 218 vertices with no K7 and no independent set of size 8 proves the bound.
